messages.subject: axes scaling in subplots
parts:
Hi all,

Does anyone have any advice on what is the best way to ensure that axes in stacked graphs are aligned?
For example, to make corresponding X values in this example appear on top of each other:

x11()
d <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=1:10,z=(1:10)*1e6)
vp1 <- viewport(width=1,height=0.5,x=0,y=1,just=c("left","top"));
vp2 <- viewport(width=1,height=0.5,x=0,y=0.5,just=c("left","top"));
g1 <- ggplot(data=d,aes(x=x))+geom_line(aes(y=y))
g2 <- ggplot(data=d,aes(x=x))+geom_line(aes(y=z))
print(g1,vp=vp1)
print(g2,vp=vp2)

Also -- is there any way to specify a formatting string for the tick labels, without having to manually compute both breaks and labels? Or, alternatively, to access the automatically determined breaks and modify their labels?

Thanks!

--aj

> x11()

> vp1 <- viewport(width=1,height=0.5,x=0,y=1,just=c("left","top"));

> g1 <- ggplot(data=d,aes(x=x))+geom_line(aes(y=y))
> g2 <- ggplot(data=d,aes(x=x))+geom_line(aes(y=z))
> print(g1,vp=vp1)
> print(g2,vp=vp2)
>

Why not use ggplot's built-in faceting capability?

d.m <- melt(d, measure.vars=c("y", "z"))
p <- ggplot(d.m, aes(x=x, y=value)) + geom_line() +
facet_grid(variable~., scales="free")
p

> Also -- is there any way to specify a formatting string for the tick labels,
> without having to manually compute both breaks and labels? Or,
> alternatively, to access the automatically determined breaks and modify
> their labels?

There are a few built-in formatters -- see help.search("formatter",
package="ggplot2") but other than that I think you do have to specify
the breaks in order to change the labels.

Best,
Ista
